column1: # The checks of shell/driver-sample.nsh: in the scenario shell-driver-sample, DriverSample
# creates its variables MyIfrNVData and MyEfiVar boot-service-only (NV+BS), which Linux
# cannot reach, and declares no PASSWORD question, so set writes without
# How old are you? (Step) has no question Flags
# and the defaults 18 and 19 of MyStandardDefault and MyManufactureDefault
# How old are you? (Step) is the byte at 0x55

column3: . == {"error_message": "no question \"No such question anywhere\" in the HiiDB"}
^error: the following required arguments were not provided:$
type == "array" and any(.[]; .name == "How old are you? (Step)" and .answer == "42")

column1: # variable list lists the boot-service-only variables of DriverSample too, sorted by name, then

column3: type == "array" and . == sort_by(.name, .guid) and any(.[]; . == {"name": "MyIfrNVData", "guid": "A04A27F4-DF00-4D42-B552-39511302113D"}) and any(.[]; . == {"name": "Timeout", "guid": "8BE4DF61-93CA-11D2-AA0D-00E098032B8C"})
. == {"error_message": "vendor A04A27F4 is not a GUID: GUID string has wrong length (expected 36 bytes)"}

column1: # variable info tells the attributes and size that dmpstore shows: NV+BS, 0xDC
# variable storage tells what QueryVariableInfo() does, by default of NV+BS+RT variables
# runtime access implies boot service access (UEFI 2.10 §8.2.3)

column3: . == {"error_message": "RUNTIME_ACCESS: runtime access implies boot service access (UEFI 2.10 section 8.2.3)"}

column1: # the help names no command or flag of the Linux build only
# get and set use the HII database here, with no backend to identify

column3: ^  get +Get the current value of a question$
^  variable +Commands on this machine's EFI variables

column1: # get and set by keyword through EFI_CONFIG_KEYWORD_HANDLER_PROTOCOL (UEFI 2.11 §35.3.1):
# DriverSample's "My Keyword Namespace Test" has the x-UEFI-ns keyword iSCSIBootEnable, the byte at
# 0x5B, with the options 0, 1 and 3; PATH is the vendor device path of DriverSample's main form set

column3: ^  keyword +Get and set the keywords of UEFI configuration languages

column1: # DriverSample's inventory list holds the keyword's string too, but none of its questions
# a <Filter> (UEFI 2.11 §35.2.1.6), which the IFR applies: iSCSIBootEnable's question is a
# read-write UINT8 ONE_OF (edk2-stable202608 DriverSampleDxe Vfr.vfr:283-290), so ReadOnly and
# Buffer pass none of its instances

column3: . == {"error_message": "keyword iSCSIBootEnable: no question of it passes the <Filter> of KEYWORD=iSCSIBootEnable&ReadOnly: PATH=01041400f4274aa000df424db55239511302113d7fff0400: ReadWrite&Numeric:1"}
. == {"error_message": "keyword iSCSIBootEnable: no question of it passes the <Filter> of KEYWORD=iSCSIBootEnable&Buffer: PATH=01041400f4274aa000df424db55239511302113d7fff0400: ReadWrite&Numeric:1"}

. == {"error_message": "expected KEYWORDINFO=, then a <Filter> (ReadOnly or ReadWrite, then Buffer, Numeric[:1|:2|:4|:8], String, Boolean, Date or Time), each optional, then the end of the <KeywordRequest>, found \"Numeric:3\""}

column1: # passes ReadWrite&Numeric:1 (ValidateFilter), and its ExtractFilter knows no Boolean, which the
# next ExtractDevicePath refuses as malformed, Progress at the '&' before it
# SetData() would store 2, which no option holds: uefisettings refuses before it calls SetData()

column3: . == {"error_message": "keyword iSCSIBootEnable: VALUE=02 is no option of question \"My Keyword Namespace Test\""}

column1: # the x-UEFI-ns keyword xUefiHiiOption (Vfr.vfr's QuestionXUefiKeywordRestStyle) has the options
# 0, 1 and 3 too: its VALUE of no option leaves iSCSIBootEnable's 3, before it, unwritten

column3: . == {"error_message": "keyword xUefiHiiOption: VALUE=02 is no option of question \"x-UEFI HII Option\""}

column1: # KEYWORDINFO (UEFI 2.11 §35.2.1.6), while VALUE is still 01: the IFR tells the question's
# <KeywordInfoResp>, UINT8, of the options 0, 1 and 3 in their en-US texts, DEFAULT on 1, and
# no manufacturing or safe default (edk2-stable202608 DriverSampleDxe Vfr.vfr:283-290,

column3: . == [{"namespace": "x-UEFI-ns", "path": "01041400f4274aa000df424db55239511302113d7fff0400", "keyword": "iSCSIBootEnable", "value": "01", "read_only": false, "data_type": "Numeric:1", "options": [{"value": "00", "string": "My one-of text #1"}, {"value": "01", "string": "My one-of text #2"}, {"value": "03", "string": "My one-of text #3"}], "standard_default": "01", "display_name": "My Keyword Namespace Test"}]
. == {"error_message": "KEYWORDINFO=\"Bogus\" is not <KeywordInfoFilter>: All, or DataType, ValueAttribute, Default and DisplayName in this order"}

column1: # GetData() of KEYWORDINFO, which edk2-stable202608 ConfigKeywordHandler.c refuses
# SetData() would write iSCSIBootEnable's byte twice, one <ConfigResp> after the other:
# uefisettings refuses before it calls SetData()

column3: . == {"error_message": "keywords iSCSIBootEnable and iSCSIBootEnable write overlapping bytes of EFI variable MyIfrNVData-a04a27f4-df00-4d42-b552-39511302113d, which SetData() writes one after the other"}

column1: # DriverSample declares no volatile VarStore: --allow-volatile writes MyIfrNVData, which is
# non-volatile, and its <KeywordResp> names no volatility
# the placeholders of the help texts, each check up to a space, where clap may wrap the line
